findings.claim: BINARIES.json is incomplete and the basis of amendment A5.1 is not logged.
findings.evidence: Target dir v22/ holds four runners: a (sha 5aa0fa91..., mtime 21:47:06, named in all 22 x1 log headers), b (sha acdbdf9c..., 22:02:03, facade constant 8, no ac2dr family; not in any log or record), c (aee3eaf3..., 22:19:58, i.e. built 5.5 min before commit a2e8e430 that BINARIES.json names), d (739e398c...). A5.1 states one ac2d 8 run lasts about 3 ms; no log holds that figure (no ac2d 8 log in banded_solve/logs or the orchestrator scratch). No tag-c log predates A5.1, the c1 data are consistent with the rationale (about 0.84 ms CPU per integration), and A5.1 changes no threshold.
findings.correction: List runner-a and runner-b in BINARIES.json with hash and use (state what runner-b ran, if anything), say runner-c was built from the working tree that became a2e8e430, and record where the 3 ms figure came from.

findings.claim: Two rulings were made after data were seen. Neither moves a threshold, and both follow the frozen text.
findings.evidence: The validity correction (cb9f36d0, after index 2) stops counting the two footer-less logs (warm-up runs only, stopped on host load and lock contention) as differences; the earlier code would have returned validity false, which means KILL. The frozen rule names differences between kernels, and my implementation of it finds none. The quiet-host timing of the third measurements made the cells of widths 12, 32 and 64 decidable; the wait read only load and lock, and the third acstrip5 measurement (1.032) set W = 6 rather than 5. Thresholds 0.95/0.03/1.00/0.60/0.75, load 8 and spread 0.10 are unchanged since the freeze.
findings.correction: None to the verdict; keep both rulings visible in the results section, as now.

findings.claim: The scope of W is narrower than the documentation states.
findings.evidence: W rests on symmetric strips at n about 8192, measured on one host and one pinned core. At w = 6 the cycle margins below 0.95 are 0.025 (acstrip, authoritative only at measurement 2; measurement 1 gave 0.805) and 0.038 (brstrip). The frozen confirmation tests band 8 at n = 64 only, so bands 6-7 at small n, asymmetric bands with both sides >= 6, and other CPUs were not measured. With the instruction criterion alone W would be 3, so cycles decide widths 3-5. The doc comment of BANDED_SLICES_MIN_HALF_WIDTH says 'every scanned problem' without naming the host.
findings.correction: State the host, core and family scope of W in REPORT_KO.md, the ledger claim and the constant's documentation.

findings.claim: D3 and D2 leave some coverage gaps. None of them changes a result.
findings.evidence: verify.sh did not run six integrator targets that call the banded driver (a1_zero_tolerance_scale, lrs_block_solver_contracts, lrs_photon_fv_contracts, lrs_photon_remap_contracts, spd01_overhead, sphere_photon_fv_contracts); I ran them at HEAD with both sentinels: 111 passed. The D2 golden has no banded SparseJvp provider and no (5,5)/(7,7) band; the boundary W-1/W is covered only by the_kernel_changes_at_the_declared_width (scalar endpoint). The provisional run w8a (sentinel g3 and clippy failures) is kept in the logs but is not mentioned in the report.
findings.correction: Optional: add the six targets to verify.sh; mention w8a in the report.
